text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:

- Prime ministers of Hungary, Italy and Slovenia signed an agreement on mutual cooperation in Budapest. The agreement expressed Slovenia's and Hungary's hopes of joining NATO in the first round of its expansion.
- Slovenia's Constitutional Court is expected to say on Thursday whether ratification of the nation's EU association agreement, signed last June, is in line with the constitution.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler ended a visit to Poland with talks with Polish Defence Minister Stanislaw Dobrzanski.
- Passenger traffic on Slovenian railways was unaffected on the first day of a 10-day strike by railway workers. Cargo traffic will be stopped again on Wednesday.
- Slovenia's largest petrol trading company Petrol has demanded price rises of between two and six percent for oil products.
- Brewer Union starts its biggest investment so far. Construction of a new warehouse is expected to cost 55 million marks.
- Prices of new cars will be up to 16 percent higher from the start of July, when new taxes come into effect.
- Tourism sales in the first three months of this year rose by two percent to $252,466 million compared to the same period in 1996, the Bank of Slovenia said.
